newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai reiterates ban on bank money in stocks.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai reiterates ban on bank money in stocks.

text.p: The People's Bank of China has repeated its warning to provincial brokerages trading in Shanghai not to handle state bank funds looking to move into stocks, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.
The central bank has ordered state banks to offset their existing stock positions by this Friday and to stop trading on the state debt repo market to help cool down the overheated stock markets.

"The provincial brokerages are not directly administered by the Shanghai government, and other provinces usually do not implement the central government's policies as strictly or as quickly as Shanghai," said one local broker.
"So the Shanghai authorities have repeated the warning to make sure these provincial brokerages are aware of it," he said.

The newspaper quoted a note from the central bank's Shanghai office as saying no subsidiary of securities houses and trust and investment companies are allowed to borrow money from banks for trading stocks.

The subsidiary offices must deposit customers' trading capital into banks and cannot use customers' capital to trade for themselves, it said, adding that money already diverted into stocks must be returned.
The branch brokerage offices are also not permitted to trade stocks for themselves, and their existing stock positions must be closed out by Friday, the newspaper said.
